prompt:
Add a streak report per habit. It runs as `python -m habitlog.streaks HABITS OUTPUT [--as-of DAY]`. HABITS is a habit file in the format the weekly command reads, and DAY is written as YYYY-MM-DD.

The as-of day is DAY. It may be left out, both on the command line and when other code calls the function that works out the streaks; then the as-of day is the latest day in HABITS. Entries after the as-of day are ignored. A habit counts once per day, even when it is listed twice on that day.

For every habit with at least one entry on or before the as-of day, work out a streak record that other code can use. The record holds the habit name; current, the number of consecutive days that end on the as-of day on which the habit was done (0 when it was not done on the as-of day); longest, the highest number of consecutive days on which it was done; total, the number of days on which it was done; and last, the latest day on which it was done. The new module should offer a function that takes the entries of the habit file and the as-of day and gives back the streak records, sorted by habit name.

If HABITS has no entries, or the as-of day is earlier than the first day in HABITS, that function must report this to its caller, and the command then exits with status 2 and does not write OUTPUT.

Write OUTPUT as JSON with two keys: "as_of", the as-of day as YYYY-MM-DD, and "habits", a list with one object per streak record, sorted by habit name, with the keys "habit", "current", "longest", "total" and "last" (the day as YYYY-MM-DD).

If DAY is not a valid day, or HABITS cannot be read or has an invalid line, the command also exits with status 2 and does not write OUTPUT. Otherwise it exits with status 0.

Add tests for the new feature.
